 This application coming on for admission this day, the c
 following:
 Order

This is first application for grant of anticipatory bail under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 on behalf of the applicant who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.314/2023 dated 25.08.2023 registered at Police Station Baikunthpur, District Rewa, for an offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 120-B, 34 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The applicant is a permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence.
The applicant is willing and ready to abide by all the directions and conditions to be imposed by this Court.
Therefore, it is prayed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
This anticipatory bail application has been argued on the ground that applicant was not named in the FIR and he is implicated in the case only on the basis of memorandum of co-accused.
It has also been argued that a compromise was arrived at between the complainant and co-accused resulting into his acquittal.

Considering these facts and also the nature of allegations made against applicant involving offence of Sections 420, 406, 120-B, 34 of IPC, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of with the direction that before taking any coercive action against applicant notice under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C. shall be served upon him.
Accordingly, the M.Cr.C. is disposed of.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE rv Abhijeet Singh @ Bablu Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60986898/
